html:
Parakramabahu I was king of Sri Lanka from 1153 to 1186, ruling from Polonnaruwa. He is the greatest of the island's medieval kings, remembered above all for his reservoirs.

The island had been split into three kingdoms since the Chola occupation ended in 1070 (see Rajendra I). Parakramabahu, a prince of one of them, fought his cousins for years and by about 1155 ruled the whole island.

The dry north and east of Sri Lanka grow rice only if the rain of a few months is stored. The chronicle has him say that not one drop of water that falls from the sky should reach the sea without serving people. It credits him with building or repairing more than 160 large reservoirs and thousands of small ones. The largest, the Sea of Parakrama at Polonnaruwa, has a bank 14 kilometres long and is still in use.

He rebuilt Polonnaruwa as a walled city of palaces, monasteries and hospitals. The great rock-cut Buddhas of the Gal Vihara were carved in his reign. He forced the island's quarrelling Buddhist orders into one, which set the pattern of Theravada Buddhism in Sri Lanka and later in Burma and Thailand.

He also sent a fleet against Burma and an army into south India. The cost was heavy, and the kingdom declined soon after his death.
sum: Parakramabahu I was king of Sri Lanka from 1153 to 1186, ruling from Polonnaruwa. He is the greatest of the island's medieval kings, remembered above all for his reservoirs.
